senses.gloss:
Vaṅga, the designation of Bengal proper is not found in the
earlier Vedic literature unless it is to be recognized in the
curious word Vaṅgāvagadhāḥ, which occurs in the Aitareya
Āraṇyaka,^1 and which suggests amendment to Vaṅga-Magadhāḥ,
‘the Vaṅgas and the Magadhas,’ two neighbouring peoples.
The name is certainly found in the Baudhāyana Dharma Sūtra.^2
1) ii. 1, 1. Cf. Keith, Aitareya Āraṇ-
yaka, 200; Magadha-Vaṅga-Matsyāḥ
occurs in the Atharvaveda Pariśiṣṭas
(i. 7, 7). but that is very late.
2) i. 1, 14. Cf. Oldenberg, Buddha,
394, n.; Calan Zeitschrift der Deutschen
Morgenländischen Gesellschaft, 56, 553.

Vaṅgṛda is the name of a demon or a human foe in the
Rigveda.^1
1) i. 53, 8. Cf. Ludwig, Translation of the Rigveda, 3, 149.
